title: Has World War III Already Started?
summary: A veteran commentator argues World War 3 began with Russia's attacks on Ukraine in 2014 or 2022 and is fought mainly through information war, while Russian nuclear use is unlikely.

assertions.quote: I'm actually of the opinion that World War III began two years ago
so you can certainly say that we are at war with Russia right now

verdicts.note: The US and Europe arm and fund Ukraine in a proxy role, but are not belligerents fighting Russia directly.
RAND describes the US arming Ukraine while explicitly ruling out direct intervention and working to avoid any direct exchange of fire with Russia, so the West is a backer, not a combatant.

DDIS assesses that Russia is waging a hybrid war against NATO and the West below the threshold of armed conflict and sees itself in conflict with the West; that is hostility short of war, and it runs from Russia to the West.

UCDP codes the Ukraine war as an interstate conflict between Russia and Ukraine only, while it does list the UK and US as warring parties in the Red Sea conflict with Yemen, so by its criteria Western states are not parties.

assertions.quote: Russia is conducting influence operations to convince you that Ukraine is not worth supporting
a war to convince you that standing up to the bear will cause World War III

verdicts.note: RAND notes Moscow has threatened but not used nuclear weapons and that public alliance disagreement could feed Russian perceptions that threatening escalation can coerce NATO over its support to Ukraine.

EFIS says Russia's arsenal and 'loud nuclear sabre-rattling' are its only real leverage to appear an equal and to push limits on NATO activity, which is coercion broader than deterring aid to Ukraine.
US intelligence records that since the invasion Russia has levied nuclear threats against the US and NATO and deployed nuclear weapons to Belarus.

assertions.quote: so there's really no tactical reason to use a nuclear weapon in Ukraine

verdicts.note: Dispersed forces and pervasive surveillance leave few massed targets where a tactical nuclear weapon would change the battle, a view many analysts share.

RAND finds troops untrained for a nuclear battlefield, slow tactical readiness and nearby own forces give Russia 'a very high bar to battlefield nuclear use', but it might still use them to signal or to stop a collapse.

assertions.quote: Russia use a nuclear weapon against advancing Ukrainian forces if they broke through Russian lines and tried to to cut off Crimea again probably not

verdicts.note: XPT forecasters made Russia the most likely user of nuclear weapons against a nuclear power by 2030 (1.87% experts, 1% superforecasters) and said the risk rises if it cannot win in Ukraine conventionally: a raised risk, not a likely response.

RAND's expert workshops find Russian nuclear escalation highly plausible and the most likely trigger a perception that battlefield losses threaten the regime, but stress Russia has a very high bar to battlefield use and may well avoid it even facing collapse.

US intelligence expects Moscow to keep to the norm against large-scale nuclear use 'absent a significant shift in its conflict with Kyiv', which leaves use under a reversal possible but not predicted.

assertions.quote: any nuclear weapons used by Russia would almost guarantee the use of nuclear weapons from NATO

verdicts.note: Russia has not used nuclear weapons despite battlefield defeats, consistent with deterrence, though NATO has signalled a conventional rather than nuclear response.

RAND finds acute fear of NATO military capabilities and reactions is one of three factors restraining Russian escalation, though it credits NATO's overall power rather than its nuclear arsenal specifically.

assertions.quote: so the Spectre of World War I has been around since the end of World War II

verdicts.note: Warnings of an imminent third world war appear in press and official statements from 1945 onward, and none has yet come true.
